messages:
OncallBot: :rotating_light: High error rate & latency spike detected on routing-service.smart-route at 1768881234. 99th p90 latency for /v1/generate rose from 160ms -> 1.4s and error rate (500) jumped from 0.2% -> 6% across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Auto-fallback attempts observed.

Alex K: I see the alert, paging oncall. Potentially related to routing fallback churn — last deploy was the smart-routing policy tweak (policy id: SR-2026-03).

Maria G: Severity? Customer-facing? @Customer Success please chime in.

Customer Success: We're already getting a few CSM threads — two mid-market customers (acme-analytics, nota-banking) reporting timeouts on tool-calling requests. Customer impact: function/tool calls failing intermittently, model outputs missing tool_call blocks.

SRE Pager: @Kevin L you are on-call for eng-sre, can you take lead?

Kevin L: Taking. Looking at routing logs now. Early hypothesis: routing negotiation is picking a quantized variant (q4_0) that does NOT expose tool_calling capability; fallback logic then routes to other regions creating a loop as variants disagree on compatibility.

Kevin L: Debug dump from routing decision API:

```
# curl -s -XPOST https://routing.internal/debug/decide -d '{"model_request": {"task":"tool_call","context_len":400,"preferred_region":"eu-west-1"}}'
{
  "decision": "route",
  "chosen_region": "eu-west-1",
  "variant": "v4-q4_0",
  "variant_features": ["quantized","fp4-compatible"],
  "tool_calling": false,
  "fallback_policy": {
    "on_incompatible_variant": "fallback-by-region",
    "max_hops": 5
  }
}
```

Kevin L: Then the next hop returned:

```
{ "chosen_region": "us-west-2", "variant": "v4-fp16", "tool_calling": true }
```

Kevin L: So the router sees eu-west offering q4 variant without tool_calling, triggers fallback to us-west, which offers fp16 with tool_calling, but our compatibility matrix incorrectly marks q4 as 'maybe-compatible' for certain context lengths. The negotiation layer oscillates because fallback creates a new routing request that again may pick the original region due to cost preference. Looping until max_hops.

Elaine R: I'm attaching a slice of routing metrics showing hop count and increased tail latency: hop_count histogram shifted to mean 2.8 -> 4.6, and error code 429/500 mix.

OncallBot: Incident creator: routing-service.smart-route | policy SR-2026-03 | triggered at 1768881234. Paging eng-sre and eng-runtime.

Maria G: Immediate mitigation options? Can we disable automated cross-region fallback or reduce max_hops to 1?

Kevin L: We can toggle the fallback policy to 'fail-fast' for the affected policy id to stop oscillation. Plan: 1) set SR-2026-03.fallback_policy.max_hops=1 2) add a temporary rule: fail if chosen_variant.tool_calling==false for tool_call requests 3) pin known affected customers to a stable fp16 variant in their region.

Alex K: I'll prepare the emergency config change. Applying canary to one routing pool in eu-west-1 first.

Kevin L: Running the change now:

```
# set via ops-config
opsctl set routing-policy SR-2026-03 --set fallback.max_hops=1 --env canary=eu-west-1
opsctl set routing-policy SR-2026-03 --set rules[tool_call].require_tool_calling=true --env canary=eu-west-1
```

OncallBot: Config change applied to canary pool (eu-west-1) at 1768881290. Monitoring...

Elaine R: Canary shows immediate drop in hop_count and errors in eu-west-1, p95 latency back to ~220ms. Canary looks good. Rolling to full policy in 2 mins.

Kevin L: Rolling to full: opsctl set routing-policy SR-2026-03 --set fallback.max_hops=1 --set rules[tool_call].require_tool_calling=true --env prod.

OncallBot: Policy updated in prod at 1768881345. Error rate decreasing.

Customer Success: Reached out to acme-analytics and nota-banking with temporary workaround (pin to fp16 variant). They confirmed reduced errors after pin.

Alex K: Root cause notes so far: compatibility matrix entries for q4 variants were missing explicit tool_calling capability flag for certain model families and context length thresholds. Negotiation treats absent flag as unknown -> allowed -> leads to incompatibility at runtime. Two bugs: 1) Missing tool_calling flag for quantized variants. 2) Compatibility comparator logic allowed fallback loops when regions had differing cost preferences and max_hops >1.

Kevin L: I also found a regression in the compatibility checker from last week where context_length check used \"<=\" instead of \"<\" causing models at boundary (e.g., 4096 tokens) to be misclassified as compatible. Patch candidate ready.

Elaine R: Mitigation checklist completed: - Fallback set to fail-fast (done) - Rule enforcing tool_calling for tool requests (done) - Affected customers pinned to fp16 variants (done) - Monitoring dashboards updated with new alarm for routing hop oscillation (done)

Maria G: Declaring incident mitigated for customer impact; keep investigating until full RCA. Severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 1768881400.

Kevin L: Next steps / follow-ups: - Patch compatibility comparator and deploy to staging (owner: Kevin L) - Update model compatibility matrix source (owner: Alex K) to include explicit capability flags for quantized builds and boundary context tests - Add unit tests to prevent context-length boundary regressions (owner: Elaine R) - Review routing policy default max_hops across all policies (owner: Maria G)

SRE Pager: Noted. Will schedule follow-up with eng-runtime and model-onboarding to validate flags for upcoming quantized variants.

Customer Success: Final status update: impacted customers experienced degraded tool-call reliability for ~12 minutes; workaround applied and no data loss. CS will follow up with postmortem customer note.

OncallBot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 1768881448. Please add tags: routing, fallback-loop, compatibility-matrix, quantization, tool-calling.

Alex K: I'll open the formal postmortem doc and link the timeline + config diffs. ETA for draft: EOD today.

Maria G: Great job triaging. Closing thread for live mitigation; keep postmortem discussion in #postmortems once doc is ready. :thumbsup:
